items.title: NEW WHITE PAPER: Deep learning for advanced users | Imaging and Machine Vision Europe
items.summary:
Deep learning is now well established in machine vision and is widely used across industries. It delivers recognition rates that were previously out of reach and automates applications that were once considered impractical. Yet many organisations still fail to get the full value from it, missing opportunities to raise performance and scale their AI-based applications. [...] Many machine vision applications rely on rule-based classifiers that take significant effort to configure by hand. Deep learning can reduce that effort, but only when it is trained on the right data, with the right strategy, and integrated sensibly with the systems you already have. This paper helps you avoid common pitfalls and see where the technology delivers the most value.

#### What will I learn about deep learning in machine vision?

By downloading this white paper, you will discover: [...] Hybrid systems: How deep learning and classical methods such as blob analysis work together, with a step-by-step example of inspecting bread rolls on a conveyor.
 Efficient deployment: How NPUs and GPUs can be matched to the application, including where space and cost rule out a full-size GPU.

items.title: Deep learning method maps spatial architecture of brain cancer cells
items.summary: helps the cancer cells survive treatment. [...] "One of our premises has always been that when we understand these rules, we can not only observe what the cells are doing, but we can also change what they are doing," said Mall. "We could perhaps reprogram them, and maybe push them into a state that is less malignant, less dangerous." [...] To learn from this variation, Stegle's team developed scDORI, a deep learning method that infers gene regulatory networks at single-cell resolution. By comparing how regulators and their target genes change together across more than a million cells, scDORI pinpoints which regulators steer cells towards one state or another. These predictions were the starting point for the reprogramming experiments carried out by Mall's team.

items.title: Hybrid Deep Learning for GI Imaging - EMJ
items.summary:
#### Key Summary:

 Deep learning improved gastrointestinal image classification through visual similarity and class imbalance.
 The model achieved a macro F1 score of 0.718 and a micro F1 score of 0.897.
 The findings highlighted the potential of focal loss and attention mechanisms for endoscopic image analysis. [...] Deep learning has shown promise in endoscopic image analysis, but classification performance can be undermined by imbalanced class distributions and visual similarities between different categories. These challenges can make it more difficult for models to distinguish between image classes reliably. [...] A HYBRID deep learning model improved gastrointestinal image classification by addressing visual similarity between classes and imbalanced data, achieving a macro F1 score of 0.718 and a micro F1 score of 0.897 in testing across 22 classes.

items.title: Deep-learning model predicts mortality from CTA scans
items.summary:
A deep-learning AI model can predict long-term mortality in patients by quantifying aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CT angiography (CTA)scans,according to a study published November 5 in _JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging_. [...] # Deep-learning model predicts mortality from CTA scans

Will Morton

Nov 6, 2026

 Add us as a preferred source on Google 

Article Summary

A deep learning AI model can predict long-term mortality in patients by analyzing aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CT angiography scans, completing analysis in 1.35 minutes with accuracy matching expert cardiologists and providing a novel biomarker for improved risk stratification in aortic stenosis. [...] "To our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate that deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue, with excellent agreement to expert assessments, strong concordance with histology, and excellent scan–rescan reproducibility," the group wrote.
